reason: The text describes several regular human characters—Korah, Dathan, Abiram, the 250 men, and the broader congregation of Israel—who each demonstrate spoken lines, emotions, and opinions. Korah's group directly addresses Moses and Aaron with their challenge (וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֲלֵהֶם 'you have presumed too much'), Dathan and Abiram explicitly refuse Moses' summons (לֹא נַעֲלֶה 'we will not come up') and voice grievances about leadership and the promised land. Moses himself exhibits emotional response (וַיִּחַר לְמֹשֶׁה מְאֹד 'Moses was very angry'). The congregation expresses fear (כִּי אָֽמְרוּ פֶּן־ תִּבְלָעֵנוּ הָאָֽרֶץ 'lest the earth swallow us'). These are not abstract entities but individuals with agency, dialogue, and expressed feelings about their circumstances.
